subject: Culture
title: Wedding Gift Economies
description: A 60-second lesson on Wedding Gift Economies.

hook.text: Italian weddings use 'bomboniere'—sugared almonds in bags. Five almonds mean health, wealth, joy, fertility, longevity.

buildup.text: Wedding gifts historically launched a new household. Guests contributed essentials: pots, linens, livestock.

discovery.text: Gift registries were invented by a Chicago department store in 1924 to prevent duplicate gift embarrassments.

twist.text: In many Asian cultures, cash gifts at weddings must exceed the cost per guest—or you've insulted the hosts.

climax.text: Couples now create honeymoon funds and charity registries. The gift has evolved from objects to experiences.

punchline.text: Weddings are gift economies disguised as love stories.

details.summary: Wedding gifts create micro-economies where families exchange wealth, establish alliances, and signal social status. Chinese weddings involve cash gifts (hongbao) carefully calibrated to relationship closeness. Western registry culture transformed weddings into household outfitting events.
details.whyItMatters: Wedding gift economies reveal that marriage is an economic event as much as a romantic one. The obligations created by wedding gifts persist for decades and shape social relationships.
takeaways: Chinese wedding gift amounts are carefully calibrated by relationship
Wedding registries were invented by department stores in the 1920s
Some cultures maintain lifelong ledgers of wedding gifts given and received

faq.question: How do Chinese wedding gifts work?
faq.answer: Guests give cash in red envelopes with amounts based on relationship closeness, region, and the wedding's extravagance. Close family gives the most. The amount must cover at least the per-person banquet cost.

faq.question: Who invented the wedding registry?
faq.answer: Marshall Field's department store in Chicago created the first wedding registry in 1924, allowing couples to select desired items and guests to purchase them without duplication. The concept solved a genuine problem but also commercialized weddings by channeling gift-giving through retail.
